summary: mxdriver ships obfuscated preinstall/postinstall dropper fetching and executing remote binaries
details: Package mxdriver@0.0.1 publishes as a 'GoogleDriver' Node.js Google API wrapper in its README (claiming zero dependencies and Node built-ins only), but ships byte-identical scripts/preinstall.js and scripts/postinstall.js that use obfuscator.io-style string-array + index decoder (_0x5694/_0x5c7e) to hide URLs, filenames, and shell commands. On npm install both hooks fetch two remote URLs from https://www.image.com/, write the bytes to package-local files gldriver_pre_core.exe and gldriver_pre_asset.exe, shell-execute them via a platform branch (mspaint on Windows, open on macOS, xdg-open on Linux) so any file type is handed to the OS handler, then unlink the files. The fetch destination is not the publisher's or README-stated Google API domain, there is no version pin or integrity check, the obfuscation hides the URLs and shell commands from casual inspection, and the entire download-and-execute behavior is undisclosed in the README. Duplication across both preinstall and postinstall increases execution reliability. Whatever www.image.com serves runs on the installer's machine at install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
